_note: How a team run's budget is split (BudgetPolicy in core/team/config.py, which documents each field). All values except expected_output_tokens_per_operator are placeholders, not measured, to be tuned on the dev incidents. Shares are decimal strings. director_share stays free in the run for the director's diagnosis and its one repair; auditor_share is the auditor's allocation; the rest goes to the blocks by max-min fairness over their estimated need, smallest first, each allocated just before it runs so unspent money rolls forward; expected_output_tokens_per_operator (1889) sizes that need and is measured on the smoke bundle only: the mean operator output of the second smoke record run (runs/cassettes/team_smoke.run2.json), not of inc-01 operators, which have not run live yet; with pool_covers_one_retry a block's need also holds, for its costliest task, one retry with history (the first request, a reply of the whole output ceiling at retry_reply_chars_per_token characters per token, 4.02, the 90th percentile of the inc-01 operator replies, and retry_feedback_chars of feedback, 1200, above the longest seen), so a one-slice block covers its first call and one repair; a manager keeps manager_share of its block and the rest is its operators' pool. A task may spend at most task_limit_first_rung_reservations times its first reservation plus task_limit_next_rung_reservations times that request's reservation one rung up the model ladder, so a reassignment one rung up can fit. operator_max_claims and operator_max_citations_per_claim cap one operator reply (said in the operator prompt; a reply over the claim cap is rejected and repaired, a claim over the citation cap keeps its first citations by position, before any check, with no repair); 4 and 5 are first guesses, to be tuned on the dev incidents. diagnosis_max_claims and diagnosis_max_citations_per_claim bound the director's diagnosis the same way, for every configuration: said in the diagnosis prompt, and a diagnosis over either keeps its first claims and citations by position, before any check, with no repair (first guesses, 2026-10-24). drop_duplicate_plan_tasks drops a plan task that repeats an earlier task's role and source (inc-05 run2 read orders-api.log twice); it is off only to replay runs recorded before it. low_coverage_threshold (a first guess, 2026-10-25): when the run read a smaller fraction of its planned operator slices, the audit carries the warning "low coverage: X of Y slices read" first; the verdict is not changed. manager_max_input_tokens (a placeholder) is the estimated input above which a manager consolidates its findings in batches. With pool_top_up, a block pool that cannot cover its next task's first reservation plus its retry reservation draws one extra allocation from the run's unallocated money (free in the run, less director_share and the needs of the blocks still to run), at most pool_top_up_max_ratio times its own allocation (a placeholder); the auditor's allocation is never touched and the ledger still enforces the run cap.
